source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether Earth could remain habitable if its size and gravity were very different.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Earth is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Moderate temperature from the right distance is not the only condition for habitability.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: gravity strength and atmosphere support -> conditions for life happens first, and that produces planet size.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Moderate temperature from the right distance is not the only condition for habitability is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth's right size helps it support an atmosphere, while a much larger planet would have much stronger gravity that could pull living beings down with crushing force. planet size -> gravity strength and atmosphere support -> conditions for life The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Earth's right size helps it support an atmosphere, while a much larger planet would have much stronger gravity that could pull living beings down with crushing force. If a planet has the right temperature, its size and gravity cannot affect whether life survives.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Why Earth supports life. The student must decide: Decide whether Earth could remain habitable if its size and gravity were very different. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
